result.next_step: No file was written. Tally numbers a voucher that carries no number by its voucher type; a number a voucher carries it keeps under Manual numbering, and under Automatic numbering discards, assigning its own. For that reason ComplyEaze Bridge writes a voucher into a voucher type whose voucher numbering it read as Automatic with existing numbers retained (the series reads Auto Retain; on the voucher type's screen, Retain Original Voucher No.). A voucher that carries its own number is also written into one read as Manual with duplicate numbers prevented; no voucher is written into any other. The voucher types in refused_types did not read so; observed says what was read, and under automatic its sub_method is auto_renumber, absent (Tally printed none) or unrecognised. Under Manual voucher numbering, a voucher sent without a number was seen to take a number already used, or to be refused. Under Automatic set to Renumber Vouchers, a voucher sent by import without a number and dated before existing vouchers was seen to change the numbers of vouchers already in the book, while the import's answer reported nothing altered; a voucher entered by hand with an earlier date did the same (one book, TallyPrime 7.1 Silver: by import on a Receipt and a Journal, by hand on a Receipt). ComplyEaze Bridge does not yet number vouchers itself, so it cannot write them for those voucher types. Leave the vouchers of those voucher types out and build the other vouchers again without them (from a parse_bank_statement proposals file, parse the statement again with from and to that leave out the days holding them; never rename a statement row), or build them again once ComplyEaze Bridge supports their numbering. A voucher type that was not among those Tally returned, or whose numbering settings could not be read, is not cured by that: check its name and settings with a masters read of voucher_types. Do not change a voucher to another voucher type, do not add a voucher number to it, and do not change a voucher type's voucher numbering to get past this: that is the user's decision, and it can change the numbers of vouchers already entered.
